> Control: block -1 by 1102537
> 
> r-cran-gstat is not in testing because it has never worked on s390x
> (#1102537).  The planned solution is to remove it on that architecture, but
> this may take some time because of the large dependency tree to be removed
> with it.

r-cran-gstat does not seem to have a single reverse dependency or 
reverse build dependency, r-cran-sp only recommends it.

Running the r-cran-gstat autopkgtest also during the build
(or build-depending on architecture-is-little-endian) plus
removal of the s390x binary should be sufficient to fix #1102537.

cu

messages.body_plain:
On 07/10/2025 12:48, Adrian Bunk wrote:
> r-cran-gstat does not seem to have a single reverse dependency or
> reverse build dependency,
It does have 4 autopkgtest-Depends (r-cran-raster/sp/spacetime/stars), 
and the entire point of #1112007 is that it's a bug when those are 
unsatisfiable.  I don't know whether its appropriate to disable these 
tests on s390x for now.  (If you remove those _packages_ on s390x, 
you're back to having to remove r-cran-sp's large-ish (23 direct, though 
not as large as a plain string search suggests, it isn't r-cran-spatial) 
reverse dependency tree on s390x.)

I also don't know when we plan to do the mass-removal on s390x that will 
be the longer-term solution.

#1112007 is worse since it is unsatisfiable even on amd64.

> I don't know whether its appropriate to disable these tests on s390x for now.
>...

For a tests-only issue either
  Restrictions: skip-not-installable
or
  Architecture: !s390x
should work.

r-cran-stars even has both:
  https://sources.debian.org/src/r-cran-stars/0.6-8-1/debian/tests/control
  https://sources.debian.org/src/r-cran-stars/0.6-8-1/debian/tests/autopkgtest-pkg-r.conf

> I also don't know when we plan to do the mass-removal on s390x that will be
> the longer-term solution.

I wouldn't do that for a test-only issue, unless the packages with the 
test rdeps themselves are also known to be broken.

cu
Adrian

messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] Bug#987714: Backlog, 32-bit architectures, endianness and next Bioconductor release.
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#987714: Backlog, 32-bit architectures, endianness and next Bioconductor release.
messages.body_plain:
Hi again,

what I missed in my last mail: Before we do any large scale uploads we
should decide about bug #987714 of dh-r.  I wonder whether we could
create the list of Depends in the same way as we create Build-Depends
automatically right in the source package.  This is the only idea I have
which enables auto-generation.  If I understood the suggestions inside
the bug report these are all connected to maintaining something
manually.

Kind regards
    Andreas.

Am Mon, Oct 20, 2025 at 03:46:53PM +0200 schrieb Andreas Tille:
> Hi Charles,
> 
> Am Sun, Oct 19, 2025 at 10:57:03AM +0900 schrieb Charles Plessy:
> > Hello everybody,
> > 
> > among the problems we have with our packages, there are:
> > 
> >  - we have a big backlog of new upstream releases, potentially pulling
> >    in new packages.
> 
> Yes.  I was hoping that we could attract some newcomers here since
> Debian packaging of R packages is (usually) brain dead easy since
> (nearly) fully automated.  What do you think about making some noise in
> the scientific community?
> 
> >  - we release our packages on architectures that are not supported
> >    upstream and we struggle keeping up with the porting load.
> 
> We should not attempt to support architectures that are not supported
> upstream.  I agree with the plan from Graham to get rid of these.
> 
> >  - Bioconductor releases every 6 month are costing us a lot of efforts
> >    and some of it is because of the above.
> 
> I wonder if the community sees some value in BioConductor Debian
> packages.  If not we find better ways to spent our spare time.  One
> indicator that the community does not care much is IMHO, that noone
> said:  "Hey, Debian is lagging behind.  How can I help?"
>  
> > One quick conclusion could be that our aims are not sustainable and that
> > we should instead point our users to well-maintained third-party
> > repositories.  But there are two objections to that:
> > 
> >  - We need r-cran-* and r-bioc-* packages as dependencies of non-R
> >    packages.
> 
> Defintely.  I have packaged *lots* of R packages - but never started
> with one that was not requested in some way by the dependency of a
> previously existing Debian package.
> 
> >    Although I do not have an estimate of the fraction of the
> >    current packages needed for that purpose, I expect it to be
> >    significant.
> 
> Its a moving target but the number is significant, IMHO.
>  
> >  - The very existence of sucessful third-party repositories shows that
> >    we can do it in Debian.
> 
> +1
> 
> >    Every day, our toolchain improves and makes
> >    it closer to reality.  For instance, the combination of Salsa and
> >    dgit opens the window for automated updates for packages that do not
> >    change their copyright summary and pass autopkgtests.
> 
> Interesting idea.
>  
> > Yet, in any case I do not see it possible to keep on releasing on
> > unsupported architectures as a default for our packages, given our
> > limited workforce.  It is like running a screen on thousands of packages
> > and claiming the responsibility for fixing the issues.  I only see a
> > future for it if would become a project on its own, with visibility,
> > support, and attracting newcomers.
> 
> +1 for the newcomers.
>  
> > So, I and maybe others have already proposed it in the past, and I think
> > that now is a good timing to do it:
> > 
> >  -> By default, let's have our package depend on architecture-is-64-bits
> >  -> and architecture-is-little-endian.
> 
> Fully ACK.
>  
> > This removes most of the porting challenges, although Debian's arm64 and
> > Apple's arm64 ports have some differences as we have seen earlier this
> > year.
> 
> That should be exceptions and might be helpful for upstream as well if
> exposed by testing in Debian.
>  
> > For this to happen, we will need to update all of our packages.  But
> > hundreds of them are outdated and all Bioconductor packages will need
> > to be udpated too starting from November.  I think that we can do it
> > even if it takes two monthes.
> 
> I might help from time to time (no promises).
>  
> > There are two major challenges down this road:
> > 
> >  - All the reverse dependencies become transitively dependant on 64-bit
> >    and little-endianness.  That is a lot of package removals to ask for
> >    and at the moment I do not have tools to automate that.
> > 
> >  - It can push a lot of stress on Testing and the Release team.  But
> >    maybe we can ask them to remove all the packages from Testing at
> >    the beginning of this sort of transition, and open a RC bug on the
> >    packages so that they do not migrate back until their dependencies
> >    are fixed?
> 
> Graham's suggestion sounded sensible.
>  
> > What are your thoughs, in particular about the two challenges above?
> 
> We should try somehow + make some noise about help we need.
> 
> When I announced to leave the team for my DPL term I realised that we
> have some Uploaders mentioned that are not active any more.  This should
> be cleaned up now fully (those who never responded should be removed
> since it makes no sense to have fake uploaders).
> 
> I'd welcome if we could win more new team members which should be
> doable.  To do so we probably need some team policy document like the
> Debian Med policy which step by step describes how to work inside the
> team.  This is a very helpful reading for newcomers.
> 
> Kind regards
>    Andreas.
> 
> -- 
> https://fam-tille.de
> 
> 

-- 
https://fam-tille.de

messages.body_plain:
On Tue, Sep 23, 2025 at 06:17:27PM +0100, Rebecca N. Palmer wrote:
> The upstream commit log suggests that this was a change on the server that
> this test connects to, and that this might happen quite often: 1.45.8,
> 1.45.10 and 1.45.11 are all plausibly relevant.
> https://github.com/Bioconductor/GenomeInfoDb/commits/devel/

Is this only a test breakage, or is the package itself also broken?

Is/Should r-bioc-genomeinfodbdata be used for tests?

I'm asking these stupid questions, since a frequently broken test should 
be dropped while a test indicating actual breakage relevant for the 
package would be useful (but if it breaks frequently the package might
not be suitable for stable releases).

According to debian/changelog there once was a needs-internet 
autopkgtest restriction, which seems to have gotten lost at
some point. This needs fixing if the test stays and needs
internet access.

cu
Adrian

messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1118697: r-bioc-biocgenerics: prepare r-cran-* r-bioc-* architecture transition by removing Bioc from Testing
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1118697: r-bioc-biocgenerics: prepare r-cran-* r-bioc-* architecture transition by removing Bioc from Testing
messages.body_plain:
Package: r-bioc-biocgenerics
Severity: serious
X-Debbugs-CC: debian-release at lists.debian.org

Hello everybody,

The next release of Bioconductor is planned for the end of this month.

Upstream, Bioconductor packages are regression-tested within their release
only.  As we can not take cross-release stability on our shoulders, we
have for some time made all r-bioc-* packages depend on a virtual package
called r-api-bioc-<versionnumber>.  For this reason, each Bioconductor
release causes a transition in Debian.

In addition, this year, we are planning a big change for the R packages
maintained by the r-pkg-team: we will align our support to only the
architectural features supported upstream, which are 64-bit and little-endian.
This will tangle with the Bioconductor transition.

To clear the path forward, I am opening this RC bug against
r-bioc-biocgenerics, which provides r-api-bioc-3.20 at the moment, so that the
whole Bioconductor and its reverse dependencies are removed from Testing.

While I have not been able to inspect the reverse dependency network
of Bioconductor, I am confident that it is limited to bioinformatics
packages only, as Bioconductor itself is specialised in this area.

Have a nice day,

Charles

--
